Theme

# Philosophy quotes about order

Order names cosmos, ritual, law, and the patterned stability that makes shared life possible—or oppressive.

20 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophers ask whether order is discovered in nature, imposed by rulers, or cultivated through custom. Chaos and creativity stand as its counterparts.

## In the history of philosophy

Cosmological order, Confucian ritual order, and modern bureaucratic order show how the same word travels across metaphysics and politics.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Plato](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/plato) , [Heraclitus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/heraclitus) , [Thomas Hobbes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-hobbes) , [Alfred North Whitehead](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/alfred-north-whitehead) , [Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/gottfried-wilhelm-leibniz) , [Ralph Waldo Emerson](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/ralph-waldo-emerson) , [The Great Learning](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-great-learning) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is order in philosophy?

It can mean natural regularity, social arrangement, or moral harmony—context decides which sense is meant.

### Is order always desirable?

Not if it encodes injustice; critical philosophies ask whose order and at what cost.

### Where are philosophy quotes about order?
